newsitem.title: USA: ABA backs Leach's bank muni underwriting provision.
newsitem.headline: ABA backs Leach's bank muni underwriting provision.

text.p: An American Bankers Association spokeswoman on Tuesday expressed strong support for Rep. James Leach's proposal to let banks underwrite municipal revenue bonds outside of a separate securities subsidiary.

Sarah Miller, senior government relations counsel for ABA, commented as the House Banking Committee is scheduled to begin work at 1400 EDT on a broad bill to eliminate most of the Depression era laws that separate banking from other financial services, including securities underwriting.
Currently, banks can underwrite revenue bonds, but only through separate securities subsidiaries.
One provision of the new billl, drafted by panel chairman Leach, a Republican from Iowa, would permit banks to directly underwrite municipal revenue bonds without setting up a sub.

"We're very, very supportive of this provision," Miller said. "Banks should have the flexibility (to) structure their business in what's best for each individual banking organization. To artifically carve out (revenue bonds) removes one leg of that flexibility," she said.
A recent draft of Leach's 90-page bill would require national banks to register with the SEC first before directly underwriting revenue bonds.
But Miller said the SEC registration requirement is a clerical "oversight" that will be stripped out of the bill during this week's committee action.
Miller said it is "ludicrous" to think that banks, which have been underwriting general obligation bonds without problems for years, will suddenly have problems with revenue bonds.
Miller added that with many Wall Street players exiting the muni business, there are more opportunities for muni underwriting by smaller regional firms.
But, currently, many small firms forego the option because they do not have the resources to set up separate securities subsidiaries.

"Many of our (banks') customers are state and local governments," Miller said. "We provide a full array of financial services to them. It's very frustrating to our customers and to us that we can't offer them muni revenue bond underwriting" other than through a Section 20 subsidiary, said Miller, who also serves as general counsel of the ABA Securities Association.
